关键词: Kaifeng Pingmei New Carbon Materials Technology Co., Ltd.
Middle East Mines and Mineral Industries Development Holding Company
主要内容: On January 5, 2021, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned key actors in Iran’s steel sector. The action targeted a Chinese supplier of graphite electrodes, Kaifeng Pingmei New Carbon Materials Technology Co., Ltd. (KFCC), and twelve Iranian steel producers, including Pasargad Steel Complex, Gilan Steel Complex Company, and Middle East Mines and Mineral Industries Development Holding Company (MIDHCO). These entities were sanctioned under Executive Order (E.O.) 13871, which aims to cut off revenue for the Iranian regime by targeting its steel sector. KFCC, which supplied thousands of metric tons of materials to Iranian steel companies between 2019 and 2020, was designated for its role in supporting Pasargad Steel Complex. The sanctions also included foreign-based sales agents of MIDHCO, such as GMI Projects Hamburg GmbH and World Mining Industry Co., Ltd., which are linked to Iranian steelmakers. The U.S. government emphasized that these actions are part of its broader strategy to deny financial support to the Iranian regime and its associated activities. The U.S. Department of the Treasury has sanctioned Darya Arya Shipping Company and its principal executive officer, Majid Sajdeh, under Section 1245(a)(1)(C)(II) of the Iran Freedom and Counter-Proliferation Act of 2012 (IFCA). The sanctions were imposed for the company's involvement in the sale, supply, or transfer of graphite to or from Iran, specifically to an Iranian person on the SDN List. The Treasury also sanctioned Majid Sajdeh for his role in the company. The sanctions mean that all property and interests in property of these individuals, if located in the U.S. or controlled by U.S. persons, must be blocked and reported to OFAC. U.S. persons are generally prohibited from engaging in transactions involving blocked or designated persons. Additionally, foreign financial institutions that facilitate significant transactions for these individuals may face U.S. correspondent or payable-through account sanctions.
